page: Microsoft Azure E64bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache, along with hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI for accelerated vector arithmetic and cryptographic tasks.

The configuration provides 512 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external premium remote block storage for persistent data requirements. Memory benchmarks highlight high read and write throughput, measuring 300.1 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 135.26 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing strong multi-threaded execution metrics.

Benchmark results show balanced compute behavior, with single-threaded metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench ranking in the middle tier, while multi-core performance tests such as PassMark CPU (61,270.34) and Geekbench multi-core (16,814.0) achieve top-quartile status. In data-intensive application benchmarks, the instance recorded 30,540.39 on PassMark database operations and 62.52 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Natural language generation on larger models shows lower throughput due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

Qualitatively, the E64bs_v5 offers favorable resource density for memory-bound workloads that process data directly in RAM without requiring local NVMe scratch space. The architecture is best aligned with large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, substantial data analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
